author: marketing_c
protectedRevelations: Scenario-specific recovery conclusions and institutional prescriptions

scenes.title: The part after the disaster
scenes.viewerPurpose: Look past the dramatic explosion to the morning after Ask what real survival and recovery require
scenes.composition: People grow food and repair tools after disruption
addOrChange: Begin after the shock, without blast spectacle or triumphant survival imagery.

cues.narration: Disaster films end at the explosion; the hardest questions often begin the following morning.
cues.visualAction: A grower and repairer try to continue necessary work.

cues.narration: Why the World Won’t End examines what survival would actually require after enormous shocks.
cues.visualAction: Link their tasks through the transport they both need.

scenes.title: A distant shock
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice different threats exposing different weaknesses See food medicine repair and trust as connected
scenes.composition: A distant shock interrupts a local delivery
addOrChange: Remove soot spectacle and show one blocked route with intact nearby buildings.

cues.narration: Nuclear war, solar storms, and emerging technologies expose different weaknesses in the systems we depend on.
cues.visualAction: Stop the supply route after a distant event.

cues.narration: Food, medicine, spare parts, and public trust become connected problems of recovery.
cues.visualAction: Food, medicine and parts wait while people need a distribution decision.

scenes.title: Knowledge needs hands
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recognize knowing a machine is not enough to rebuild its parts Separate losing a way of life from losing humanity
scenes.composition: A technician understands a pump but lacks a needed part
addOrChange: Use a matching component outline and empty slot, without easy rebuilding.

cues.narration: Knowing how a machine works does not mean its missing supply chain can be rebuilt.
cues.visualAction: Match the manual to the missing component and pause the repair.

cues.narration: The book separates the end of a familiar world from the end of humanity.
cues.visualAction: Widen to people continuing basic work around the unresolved machine.

scenes.title: What recovery requires
scenes.viewerPurpose: Find room for preparation without easy comfort Ask what people would need to build a life again
scenes.composition: Residents and an official plan continuity around a shared record
addOrChange: Keep one food plan, one repair need and an open discussion.

cues.narration: It asks how we might prepare without pretending that survival would be easy.
cues.visualAction: Compare possible preparations with the difficulties still unknown.

cues.narration: What must we preserve now so people could still build a life afterward?
cues.visualAction: End on the ordinary people who would need to use the preserved record.
